g.data-label: 009 D3 · faults enter through this same seam not as injected internal decisions — the state machine and driver stay production code and decide how to react provider: retryable · non-retryable · protocol-inconsistent result partial stream then error · empty terminal response tool: typed execution error · wrong call id · past-deadline completion approval: explicit denial · no response before a declared deadline every outcome also defines its logical world transition: a write-like fault says whether the update occurred, a drop updates availability, a deadline says whether work completed — timeout may not leave logical state ambiguous directly forcing StepDecision, editing ledger state, or bypassing validation is rejected — it would test a second transition system

g.data-label: 009 D4 · time crosses as a controlled dimension the world owns a monotonic clock; conformant code reads it through the seam and never reads ambient wall time where the value can affect behaviour or an asserted trace advances reject negative or overflowing movement completion-versus-deadline is a shared pure helper or a conformance- tested adapter contract, never re-derived in the generator external shell, MCP, and OS-process timeouts stay real-time and are never invoked as the clock oracle in a deterministic run

g.data-label: the driver uses the same request/response types and the same transition code in both cases · production state-machine and policy code does not branch on test mode the world ends at the external result boundary: production still validates and interprets StepResult and AIError, correlates tool-call ids, converts typed outcomes into history messages, applies approval and policy decisions, updates budgets, and records ledger events — moving any of that into the simulator would violate D5

g.data-label: 009 D5 · the profile fences the boundary an extension is covered only if every hook reachable in the profile is either deterministic and effect-free for its explicit inputs, or effectful only through world-mediated ports with explicit state returned a reached-but-excluded hook, or any direct AI · Process · Net · FS · SharedMem · Clock · env · random effect → fail closed a run cannot gain coverage credit because its seed missed a direct-effect hook capability flags are necessary but not sufficient: broad IO permits both reporting and readLine, so the gate also needs a source and ABI routing audit, poison probes per boundary, and fail-closed profile validation
